name: Relamorelin

lead: Relamorelin (RM-131) is an investigational injected ghrelin analogue. Some people group it with ghrelin-pathway compounds associated with appetite, growth hormone and lean mass.

It is a synthetic pentapeptide that activates the ghrelin receptor, which raises growth hormone and appetite. It was developed to speed stomach emptying in diabetic gastroparesis, and phase 2 trials reported faster emptying and less vomiting. It was also studied in constipation and anorexia nervosa. Phase 3 trials registered in 2017 and 2018 were all later terminated.

paras: It has been given as a subcutaneous injection inside clinical trials only. It is not sold as a product.
It is not approved anywhere. Safety data come from clinical trials in gastrointestinal and eating-disorder patients, and no studies have tested it for appearance.

angle.text: Relamorelin activates the ghrelin receptor to raise appetite and growth hormone signalling, and some link that to more lean mass and a fuller look. It was studied for diabetic gastroparesis, and no appearance data exist.

lead: Relamorelin (RM-131) is a synthetic pentapeptide ghrelin analogue that is injected subcutaneously. It was developed to treat diabetic gastroparesis, a condition of delayed stomach emptying, and was also studied in constipation and anorexia nervosa.[1][2][3]

Its phase 2 trials reported faster gastric emptying and reduced vomiting in diabetic gastroparesis.[2][3] Several phase 3 trials were registered in 2017-2018 and all were later terminated.[4][5][6][7][8] Wikipedia describes its development status as uncertain.[1]
No studies have tested relamorelin for appearance or muscle-building purposes.

paras: Relamorelin is a centrally penetrant, selective agonist of the ghrelin receptor with improved potency and pharmacokinetics compared with ghrelin.[1][9] In humans, receptor agonists of this kind raise growth hormone, prolactin and cortisol and increase appetite.[1] In healthy volunteers it affected gastric motor functions and satiation.[10]

A phase 2 trial of 204 patients with diabetic gastroparesis reported that relamorelin reduced vomiting frequency and severity and accelerated gastric emptying.[2] A 12-week phase 2B study of 393 patients assessed symptoms and gastric emptying.[3][11] Smaller studies examined chronic constipation, Parkinson disease with constipation, and anorexia nervosa, including a randomised trial in outpatient women with anorexia nervosa.[12][13][14][15] Five phase 3 diabetic gastroparesis studies enrolling 202-467 participants were registered between 2017 and 2018, and all are listed as terminated.[4][5][6][7][8]

A phase 1b study in 2013 tested it in women with type 2 diabetes and delayed gastric emptying, and the FDA granted Fast Track designation for diabetic gastroparesis.[1] Wikipedia notes that a 2019 company filing listed an expected 2024 launch that did not appear in later filings.[1]

timeline.event: Phase 1b study in diabetic women with delayed gastric emptying.[1]
